exposure: Type of anesthesia for cesarean delivery (general anesthesia vs. epidural anesthesia)
Conversion from epidural labor analgesia to general anesthesia
outcome: Neonatal morbidity (composite of umbilical artery pH < 7.10, 5-min Apgar score < 7, and/or NICU admission)
cohort: Mother-neonate pairs who underwent intrapartum category-1 cesarean deliveries at an academic tertiary care institution
finding: Conversion of epidural analgesia to general anesthesia for category-1 cesarean delivery in women with a functional labor epidural catheter was not associated with poorer neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Conversion of epidural analgesia to general anesthesia for category-1 cesarean delivery in women with a functional labor epidural catheter is not associated with poorer neonatal outcomes.
